plan.title: bug(test): pyproject_version_freshness test flakes on a live git ls-remote (5s vitest timeout in CI)

narratives.Description: packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/pyproject_version_freshness.test.ts > test_manifest_version_matches_latest_tag intermittently times out at vitest's 5000ms budget in CI, failing the TypeScript (build + lint + test) check on otherwise-clean PRs. It is a network-timing flake, not a logic regression.
narratives.UserStory: As a contributor whose PR is otherwise green, I want the version-freshness unit test to run offline and deterministically, so a slow GitHub round-trip never times out my CI and forces a re-run.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Root cause: the test's latestReleaseTag() calls latestRemotePublishableTag('origin', repoRoot()), which at packages/core/src/platform/resolve-version.ts:273 runs a synchronous network call execFileSync('git', ['ls-remote','--tags','--refs','--', remote]). Under CI load this exceeds vitest's 5s testTimeout. 2. Remove the live-remote dependency from the TEST path (pick the cleanest): (a) resolve the tag locally only in the test via latestLocalPublishableTag(repoRoot()) (git describe / git tag --list -- local + fast), keeping the existing early-return-when-null behavior; OR (b) inject a seam so the test supplies an offline/fake tag resolver (no execFileSync in the unit test); OR (c) add a bounded timeout to latestRemotePublishableTag and have the test tolerate null/timeout gracefully. 3. The assertion is already best-effort (`if (!tag || manifestVersion === '0.0.0') return`), so dropping the network leg loses ~no coverage. 4. Keep the production resolve-version.ts remote helper behavior unchanged for real release tooling (if you add a timeout param, make it additive + covered). 5. Ensure the whole test file runs well under 1s with no network. 6. Run repo-root pnpm run lint (full-file lane) + task check.
narratives.Overview: See https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2256. On PR #2249 the check failed with 'Test timed out in 5000ms' for test_manifest_version_matches_latest_tag; 8256/8257 passed and a re-run went green. Same flaky class as #2209/#2219 (wall-clock/network dependence in a unit test). The culprit is a synchronous git ls-remote origin inside the test. Fix: make the unit test offline/deterministic.
narratives.GuardRails: TS-native repo, vitest. Do NOT change production release-tooling behavior of latestRemotePublishableTag (real release flows still need the remote lookup) -- scope the fix to the TEST path (or an additive, tested timeout). Do NOT mark the test skipped as the fix -- it must still assert freshness when a tag is locally resolvable. Keep it offline; a shallow clone with no tags should early-return cleanly, not fail.

items.title: test_manifest_version_matches_latest_tag runs offline and deterministically (no git ls-remote / network in the test path).
The test still verifies manifest-vs-tag freshness when a tag is resolvable locally, and early-returns cleanly when none is available.
The whole test file runs in well under 1s with no wall-clock/network dependence that can exceed vitest's 5s budget.
Production resolve-version.ts remote helper behavior is unchanged for real release tooling (or any timeout added is additive + tested).
